translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Uyghurs raided Taiyuan and Bao Fang was beaten.

sentences.zh: 朱泚徙封遂寧郡王。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Suining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was retitled Prince of Suining.

sentences.zh: 二月庚辰，代州都督張光晟擊回紇，戰於羊武谷，破之，北人乃安。

translations.literal: Second month, gengchen: Dai prefect Zhang Guangcheng struck Uyghurs at Yangwu Valley and broke them; the northerners were then calm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Zhang Guangcheng routed the Uyghurs at Yangwu Valley.

sentences.zh: 己亥，吐蕃寇靈武。

translations.literal: On jihai, Tibet raided Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Tibet raided Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，太僕寺佛堂有小脫空金剛右臂忽有黑汁滴下，以紙承之，色類血。

translations.literal: On jiachen, at the ministry of imperial stud's Buddha hall a small hollow gilt guardian's right arm suddenly dripped black fluid; paper caught it—the color was like blood.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, black fluid like blood dripped from a gilt guardian's arm in the stud's Buddha hall.

sentences.zh: 三月甲戌，河陽將士劫回紇輜重，因與相鬥，縱兵大掠，久之方定。

translations.literal: Third month, jiaxu: Heyang soldiers robbed Uyghur baggage, fought them, and plundered freely for a long time before order returned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Heyang troops looted Uyghur baggage, fought them, and rioted for days.

sentences.zh: 四月丁亥，以浙西觀察留後李道昌為蘇州刺史、兼御史中丞，充浙西都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Fourth month, dinghai: Zhexi acting observation commissioner Li Daochang was made Suzhou prefect, concurrent acting censor-in-chief, and Zhexi all-training observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Li Daochang became Suzhou prefect and Zhexi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以前浙西觀察使李涵為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On jichou, former Zhexi commissioner Li Han was made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Li Han became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，吐蕃寇靈州，朔方留後常謙光擊敗之。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Tibet raided Lingzhou; Shuofang acting commissioner Chang Qianguang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Tibet raided Ling and Chang Qianguang drove them off.

sentences.zh: 五月戊午，宦官劉清潭賜名忠翼。

translations.literal: Fifth month, wuwu: eunuch Liu Qingtan was granted the name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the eunuch Liu Qingtan received the name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 六月戊戌，隴右節度使朱泚於軍士趙貴家得貓鼠同乳不相害，籠而獻之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, wuxu: Longyou commissioner Zhu Ci at officer Zhao Gui's house obtained a cat and rat nursing together without harm; caged and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Zhu Ci presented a cat and rat nursing together from Zhao Gui's house.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬子，中書舍人崔祐甫知吏部選事。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renzi: drafting secretary Cui Youfu was put in charge of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Cui Youfu took charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，劍南節度使崔寧加檢校司空，東川李叔明加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: On guichou, Jiannan commissioner Cui Ning was made acting grand master; eastern Sichuan Li Shuming was made acting minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Cui Ning became acting grand master and Li Shuming acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 辛未，吐蕃寇鹽州、慶州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Tibet raided Yan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Tibet raided Yan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 八月甲戌朔，成德軍節度使李寶臣抗章請復本姓張氏，從之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, jiaxu new moon: Chengde commissioner Li Baochen submitted a memorial asking to restore his original surname Zhang; approved.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon, Li Baochen was allowed to resume the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁酉，葬貞懿皇后於莊陵。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, dingyou: Empress Zhenyi was buried at Zhuang tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Empress Zhenyi was buried at Zhuangling.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁卯，日長至，有司禮昊天上帝於南郊，上不視朝故也。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, dingmao: on the winter solstice the offices sacrificed to the Supreme Lord of Heaven at the southern suburb; the emperor did not hold court for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the southern suburb rites for the solstice kept the emperor from court.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙戌，以吏部尚書劉晏為左僕射，判使如故。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, bingxu: Minister of Personnel Liu Yan was made left vice director, fiscal commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Liu Yan became left vice director while keeping the fiscal portfolio.

sentences.zh: 以給事中杜亞為洪州刺史、兼御史中丞，充江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Drafting attendant Du Ya was made Hongzhou prefect, concurrent acting censor-in-chief, and Jiangxi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya became Hongzhou prefect and Jiangxi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以江西觀察使路嗣恭為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Jiangxi observation commissioner Lu Sigong was made minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sigong of Jiangxi became minister of war.

sentences.zh: 是歲，郴州黃芩山崩，壓死者有數百人。

translations.literal: That year at Huangqin mountain in Chenzhou the mountain collapsed and several hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: That year a Chenzhou landslide killed hundreds on Huangqin mountain.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年十四年春正月壬寅朔。

translations.literal: Dali 14, spring, first month, renyin new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 14 opened on the renyin new moon of the first spring month.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以楚州刺史李泌為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: On renxu, Chuzhou prefect Li Bi was made Li prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Li Bi was transferred from Chu to Li.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，魏博七州節度使、太尉、檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事、魏州大都督府長史田承嗣卒。

translations.literal: Second month, guiwei: Weibo seven-prefecture commissioner, grand master, acting left vice director, fellow grand councilor, and Wei chief administrator Tian Chengsi died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Tian Chengsi of Weibo, fellow grand councilor, died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以魏博中軍兵馬使、左司馬田悅兼御史中丞，充魏博節度留後。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Weibo central army military commissioner and left aide Tian Yue was made concurrent acting censor-in-chief and acting Weibo commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Tian Yue became acting Weibo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，汴宋節度使李忠臣為麾下將族侄李希烈所逐，忠臣狼狽歸朝。

translations.literal: Third month, dingwei: Bian-Song commissioner Li Zhongchen was driven out by his officer and clansman Li Xilie; Zhongchen fled in distress to court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Xilie expelled Li Zhongchen from Bian-Song; Zhongchen fled to court.

sentences.zh: 上以忠臣立功於國，乃授檢校司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: Because Zhongchen had merit for the state, he was made acting grand master and fellow grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court made the disgraced Zhongchen grand councilor for past service.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以河南尹嚴郢為京兆尹，河中少尹、知府事趙惠伯為河南尹。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Henan metropolitan prefect Yan Yun became capital metropolitan prefect; Hezhong junior metropolitan prefect and acting administrator Zhao Huibo became Henan metropolitan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Yan Yun became capital prefect and Zhao Huibo took Henan.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以前容管經略使、容州刺史王翃為河中少尹、知府事。

translations.literal: On xinyou, former Rongguan pacification commissioner and Rong prefect Wang Hong was made Hezhong junior metropolitan prefect and acting administrator.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Wang Hong became acting Hezhong administrator.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸未，成德軍節度使張寶臣復請姓李，從之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, guiwei: Chengde commissioner Zhang Baochen again asked to take the surname Li; approved.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Zhang Baochen was again allowed the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 五月癸卯，上不康，至辛亥，不視朝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, guimao: the emperor was unwell; until xinhai he did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: From guimao through xinhai of the fifth month illness kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 北都留守鮑防以北庭歸朝。

translations.literal: Northern capital guardian Bao Fang because the Northern Court returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fang of Taiyuan welcomed the Northern Court's return to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict had the crown prince oversee the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the crown prince was ordered to oversee the realm.

sentences.zh: 是夕，上崩於紫宸之內殿。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor died in the inner hall of Zichen.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died in the Zichen inner hall.

sentences.zh: 遺詔皇太子柩前即位。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict had the crown prince succeed before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: His will ordered the crown prince to succeed before the bier.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，遷神柩於太極殿，發喪。

translations.literal: On renxu the spirit coffin was moved to Taiji Hall and mourning was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the coffin was placed in Taiji Hall and mourning began.

sentences.zh: 八月庚申，群臣上尊謚曰睿文孝武皇帝，廟號代宗。

translations.literal: Eighth month, gengshen: the hundred officials submitted the honorific title Sagacious Culture Filial Martial Emperor; temple name Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the court gave him the posthumous title Sagacious Culture Filial Martial and temple name Daizong.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，葬於元陵。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jiyou: burial at Yuan tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou of the tenth month he was buried at Yuanling.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉，祔於太廟。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, dingyou: enshrined in the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou his tablet entered the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 【史評】史臣曰：嗚呼，治道之失也，若河決金堤，火炎昆崗，雖神禹之乘四載，玄冥之灑八瀛，亦不能堙洪濤而撲烈焰者，何也？

translations.literal: 【Historian's appraisal】The historian says: Alas, when the way of governance fails, it is like a river breaking its golden dike or fire blazing on Kunwu mountain—even if divine Yu rode the four conveyances and Dark Lord poured the eight seas, he could not dam the flood or smother the flames. Why?
translations.idiomatic: 【Historian's appraisal】The historian writes: When governance fails, it is like a breached dike or a mountain fire—even Yu himself could not hold back the flood once the breach widens. Why?

sentences.zh: 良以勢既壞而不能遽救也。

translations.literal: Truly because once the situation is ruined it cannot be swiftly rescued.
translations.idiomatic: Because once the breach opens, rescue comes too late.

sentences.zh: 觀夫開元之治也，則橫制六合，駿奔百蠻；

translations.literal: Consider Kaiyuan's governance: it held the six directions in check and made the hundred barbarians gallop;
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan the throne mastered the realm and drove the hundred tribes;

sentences.zh: 及天寶之亂也，天子不能守兩都，諸侯不能安九牧。

translations.literal: when the Tianbao disorder came, the Son of Heaven could not hold the two capitals and the feudatories could not secure the nine pastures.
translations.idiomatic: under Tianbao the emperor lost both capitals and the provinces could not keep order.

sentences.zh: 是知有天下者，治道其可忽乎！

translations.literal: Thus one knows that whoever holds the realm cannot neglect the way of governance!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds the realm cannot neglect how it is ruled.

sentences.zh: 明皇之失馭也，則思明再陷於河洛；

translations.literal: When Minghuang lost the reins, An Lushan twice seized the Yellow River lands;
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong lost control, An Lushan twice took the heartland;

sentences.zh: 大歷之失馭也，則懷恩鄉導於犬戎。

translations.literal: when Dali lost the reins, Pugu Huai'en guided the dog barbarians as native scouts.
translations.idiomatic: under Dali, Pugu Huai'en led the Uyghurs against the throne.

sentences.zh: 自三盜合從，九州羹沸，軍士膏於原野，民力殫於轉輸，室家相吊，人不聊生，而子儀號泣於用兵，元載殷憂於避狄。

translations.literal: From the three rebels' alliance the nine provinces boiled; soldiers greased the wilds and the people were spent on transport; households mourned each other and life was unbearable—yet Ziyi wept over levies and Yuan Zai grieved over fleeing barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion scorched the provinces; armies and transport drained the people—yet Guo Ziyi wept over taxes and Yuan Zai over Tibetan raids.

sentences.zh: 然而代宗皇帝少屬亂離，老於軍旅，識人間之情偽，知稼穡之艱難，內有李、郭之效忠，外有昆戎之幸利。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Daizong, young amid disorder, old in the camps, knew human deceit and the hardship of harvests; within were Li and Guo's loyalty, without the fortune of border trade with the western barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, raised in war, knew deceit and famine; he had Li and Guo within and border trade without.

sentences.zh: 遂得兇渠傳首，叛黨革心，關輔載寧，獯戎漸弭。

translations.literal: Thus the vicious chiefs sent heads and rebels changed heart; Guanfu was pacified and the steppe barbarians gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel heads came in and the frontiers quieted.

sentences.zh: 至如稔輔國之惡，議元振之罪，去朝恩之權，不以酷刑，俾之自咎，亦立法念功之旨也。

translations.literal: As for bearing Fuguo's evil, debating Yuan Zhen's crime, removing Chao'en's power without cruel punishment and making them blame themselves—this too was the intent of law that weighs merit.
translations.idiomatic: He endured Fuguo, judged Yuan Zhen, and stripped Chao'en without torture—mercy within justice.

sentences.zh: 罪己以傷僕固，徹樂而悼神功，懲縉、載之奸回，重袞、綰之儒雅，修己以禳星變，側身以謝咎徵，古之賢君，未能及此。

translations.literal: He blamed himself to mourn Pugu, ceased music to grieve Tian Shenggong, punished Jin and Zai's treachery, valued Gai and Wan's scholarship, cultivated himself to answer star omens and bowed his person to acknowledge calamities—ancient sage rulers did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Huai'en, honored Shenggong, purged Zai, elevated Gai and Wan, and humbled himself before omens—sage kings did no more.

sentences.zh: 而猶有李靈耀作梗，田承嗣負恩，命將出軍，勞師弊賦者，蓋陽九之未泰，豈君道之過歟！

translations.literal: Yet Li Lingyao still made trouble and Tian Chengsi betrayed grace; when generals marched, armies were worn and taxes exhausted—perhaps the yang ninth had not yet turned fair; how could it be only the ruler's fault!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lingyao and Chengsi still rebelled and campaigns still drained the realm—the age was not yet fair; not every fault was the emperor's alone.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：群盜方梗，諸戎競侵。

translations.literal: 【Eulogy】Bandits still blocked the roads; the many barbarians vied to invade.
translations.idiomatic: 【Eulogy】Bandits blocked the roads; barbarians pressed on every side.

sentences.zh: 猛士嘗膽，忠臣痛心。

translations.literal: Fierce warriors tasted gall; loyal ministers ached in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors braced themselves; loyal ministers grieved.

sentences.zh: 掃除沴氣，敷衍德音。

translations.literal: Sweeping away foul vapors, spreading virtuous pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: He swept away ruin and spread mercy in edicts.

sentences.zh: 延洪納祉，帝慮何深。

translations.literal: Extending great blessing and receiving blessing—how deep the emperor's concern!
translations.idiomatic: He sought blessing for the realm—how deep his care!
